title: Female Pelvis & Perineum Anatomy: Viscera & Floor Guide
description: Learn female pelvis and perineum anatomy, detailing the bladder, uterus, rectum, peritoneal pouches, levator ani muscular floor, and perineal triangle map.
h1: Female Pelvis and Perineum Anatomy: Viscera, Pouches and Pelvic Floor
blurb: Sagittal and perineal views of the female pelvis: bladder, anteverted uterus, vesicouterine and rectouterine pouches, levator ani floor, and perineal body.
lead: The female pelvis is wider and more circular than the male pelvis, cradling the bladder, uterus, and rectum above a dynamic muscular sling built for both support and childbirth. In this illustrated guide to female pelvis and perineum anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including urinary bladder, female urethra, vagina, uterus & cervix (relations)—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: The female pelvis is wider and more circular than the male pelvis, cradling the bladder, uterus, and rectum above a dynamic muscular sling built for both support and childbirth. Deep regional anatomy of the female pelvis: pouches, cardinal ligaments, pelvic floor and perineum. Within the human body, the female pelvis & perineum (Pelvis femina) is situated in pelvic sagittal section, receives arterial perfusion via internal iliac branches, and is innervated by pudendal + pelvic splanchnics.

Structurally, the urinary bladder (Vesica urinaria) comprises reservoir behind the pubic symphysis. Physiologically, the urinary bladder stores urine. The female urethra (Urethra femina) is short 4 cm tube to the vestibule. Physiologically, the female urethra governs voiding. The vagina is muscular canal from cervix to vestibule. Physiologically, the vagina governs intercourse, menstrual flow, birth canal. Structurally, the uterus & cervix (relations) (Uterus) comprises anteverted over the bladder, pouch behind. Physiologically, the uterus & cervix (relations) governs gestation and menstruation. Structurally, the vesico- & recto-uterine pouches (Excavationes) comprises peritoneal recesses front and back of uterus. Physiologically, the vesico- & recto-uterine pouches allow organ movement; collect free fluid. Structurally, the rectum comprises terminal bowel behind the vagina. Physiologically, the rectum governs stool storage.

Clinically, regarding the urinary bladder, stress incontinence follows pelvic-floor weakness. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the female urethra, short length explains higher UTI rates in women. In clinical pathology involving the vagina, anteverted uterus rests on its anterior wall; pessaries sit here. Medical evaluation of the uterus & cervix (relations) also notes that retroversion is a normal variant in ~20%.

questions.question: Which organs are located in the female pelvis?
questions.answer: The female pelvis contains the bladder, uterus, cervix, vagina and rectum; the ovaries and uterine tubes lie laterally.

questions.question: What supports the uterus and pelvic organs?
questions.answer: The levator ani and coccygeus form the pelvic diaphragm, supporting pelvic viscera and helping maintain continence; connective-tissue attachments also stabilize the uterus.

questions.question: Where is the urinary bladder in the female pelvis?
questions.answer: In the female pelvis, the bladder lies anterior to the vagina and uterus.

questions.question: Where is the vagina located?
questions.answer: The vagina is a muscular canal extending from the cervix to the vestibule.

questions.question: What do the vesicouterine and rectouterine pouches do?
questions.answer: These peritoneal recesses accommodate movement of pelvic organs and can collect free fluid.
